title: Maintained lead: get in front, stay in front
summary: How maintained lead works step by step on a crosser, which targets it often suits, and its typical fault: measuring the gap.

body.html: Maintained lead (in the US: sustained lead) keeps the muzzles in front of the target from the start to the shot. Here is how it looks, step by step, on a crosser (a target flying across in front of you):

html: Start: the barrels wait at the hold point, well out along the target’s path, so the target will fly towards them; your eyes look back towards the pick-up point.
Insertion: as the target comes, the gun moves and the muzzles join the line in front of it, not behind; this is the insertion point.

Tracking: at first the barrels move a little slower than the target, so the target catches up until the gap between them is the size you want. Then move the barrels at the target’s speed, and the gap stays the same.
Shot: the trigger is pulled while the gap is right and the gun is still moving.
After the shot the gun keeps moving (follow-through).

body.html: Strengths: precise, little gun movement, quick between targets, and the lead is easy to adjust. It suits consistent, predictable targets: long crossers, steady high targets.

Weaknesses: it is often described as the hardest method to learn, and the shooter must know the target’s speed and line in advance. Because the gun is not faster than the target, the shooter sees the biggest gap of the moving-gun methods. That tempts many shooters to measure it, slow down and stop.
Coaches say “insert the gun in front”, “stay ahead of it”, “match its speed”.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Get in front and stay in front.
phrases.meaning: Put the muzzles ahead of the target and keep them there until after the shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Your insertion point is behind the bird — put the gun in front of it.
phrases.meaning: The muzzles joined the line behind the target; they must join ahead of it.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Match its speed — don't let it catch you.
phrases.meaning: Move the gun at the target's speed so the gap does not shrink.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You're measuring it — trust the picture and pull.
phrases.meaning: The shooter is slowing down to check the gap; fire as soon as the picture is right.

key_points.html: Muzzles start ahead and join the line in front of the target.
Once the gap is right, gun speed = target speed, so the gap stays constant.
Trigger while the gap is right and the gun is moving; then follow through.
Main risk: measuring the gap and stopping the gun.

quiz.q: In maintained lead, where do the muzzles join the target's line?
quiz.explain: The muzzles are inserted ahead of the target and stay ahead; behind is swing-through, on the target is pull-away.

quiz.q: What is the typical fault of maintained-lead shooters?

options.text: Measuring the gap and stopping the gun
Shooting too early at the trap

quiz.explain: The gap is large and visible, so shooters are tempted to check it; the gun slows or stops and the shot goes behind.

quiz.q: For which target is maintained lead often recommended?

options.text: A bouncing rabbit in a short gap

quiz.explain: The method needs a known speed and line, which long, steady crossers give; erratic or surprise targets suit other methods.
